title: Error details lost in fallback chain — only generic message returned to caller
why_it_matters: When the default provider fails and all fallbacks also fail, the caller receives only 'All search providers failed' with no information about WHY each provider failed (auth, network, quota, config). This makes debugging impossible for both users and operators.

title: Google API key exposed in URL query parameter, leaked into logs and UI error messages
why_it_matters: The Google Custom Search API key is passed as a URL query parameter. When reqwest encounters a network error, its Display representation includes the full request URL, embedding the API key in the error string. This error propagates to logs and UI.

title: SSRF via unvalidated SearXNG base_url
why_it_matters: SearxngProvider::new() accepts an arbitrary base_url with only an emptiness check. No scheme validation, host allowlisting, or internal IP filtering. An attacker can set base_url to internal endpoints causing unauthorized requests.

title: Massive code duplication across 6 search provider implementations
why_it_matters: All 6 providers share nearly identical struct definitions, constructor validation, HTTP client setup, response parsing, and result mapping logic (~80% duplication). Any change requires editing 6 files.

title: SearchOptions fields language/region/date_range/safe_search are completely unused
why_it_matters: Four fields on SearchOptions are defined with documentation and serde attributes but zero providers consume them. Callers can set these values but they silently do nothing — a false API contract.

title: Failed provider test results cached for 5 minutes, hiding transient failures
why_it_matters: test_search_provider caches BOTH success and failure results with a 5-minute TTL. A transient network blip causes the provider to appear broken for 5 minutes even if recovered immediately.

title: Provider test cache not invalidated when provider configuration changes
why_it_matters: The test cache is keyed only by provider name. If a user updates an API key, the old cached test result continues to be returned for up to 5 minutes.

title: Registry search does not check is_available() before executing search
why_it_matters: search() retrieves providers and immediately calls .search() without checking provider.is_available(). A provider with an empty API key still makes an HTTP request and fails, wasting resources.

title: Google CSE max_results not capped to API limit of 10, causing API errors
why_it_matters: Google Custom Search API limits the 'num' parameter to maximum 10. The code passes options.max_results directly without validation. A request for 50 results returns 400 Bad Request.

title: timeout_seconds = 0 causes immediate request failure in all providers
why_it_matters: timeout_seconds is u64 with no validation. A value of 0 produces Duration::from_secs(0), which reqwest interprets as an immediate timeout. Every search call fails instantly.

title: Unbounded max_results allows API quota exhaustion and resource abuse
why_it_matters: max_results is a usize with no upper bound. Providers pass it directly to external APIs. An attacker can set it to usize::MAX causing excessive bandwidth consumption and rapid API quota exhaustion.

title: Mutex poison recovery in test_cache hides thread panics
why_it_matters: test_cache.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner()) silently recovers from a poisoned mutex. In Rust, mutex poisoning indicates that a thread panicked while holding the lock. However, CLAUDE.md P7 explicitly approves this pattern as the standard handling for non-critical caches.

title: SearXNG provider does not pass max_results to API, fetching all results
why_it_matters: SearXNG supports query parameters to limit results, but the provider only passes q and format. It fetches ALL results and then applies .take() client-side, wasting bandwidth and increasing latency.

title: SearXNG response deserialization missing #[serde(default)] on results field
why_it_matters: SearxngResponse.results lacks #[serde(default)]. If a SearXNG instance returns a 200 response with missing 'results' key, deserialization fails instead of being handled gracefully as an empty result set.

title: test_search_provider does not check is_available() before making API call
why_it_matters: test_search_provider finds the provider by name and immediately calls provider.search('test', ...) without checking is_available(). For an unconfigured provider, this makes an unnecessary HTTP request guaranteed to fail.

title: Inconsistent max_results enforcement across providers
why_it_matters: Providers handle max_results inconsistently: some pass it to API and trust it, some pass it AND locally truncate, and Searxng doesn't pass it at all. Same SearchOptions yields different result counts depending on provider.

title: Fragile error classification via string matching in registry
why_it_matters: Error classification in test_search_provider uses substring matching on error messages. If error messages change or providers return structured errors differently, classification breaks silently.

title: Module doc comments placed after use statements in all provider files
why_it_matters: In all 6 provider files, the module doc comment is placed after the first two use statements and before the remaining imports. This is non-idiomatic.

title: Registry tests depend on real TavilyProvider instead of mock
why_it_matters: The registry test module imports and uses the real TavilyProvider for a test that only needs any SearchProvider implementation. Creates unnecessary coupling.

title: Stringly-typed provider_type in SearchProviderTestConfig
why_it_matters: SearchProviderTestConfig.provider_type is a String with a comment listing valid values. This should be an enum for compile-time validation.

title: Duplicate module declaration pattern in mod.rs
why_it_matters: The mod.rs file declares submodules in two separate groups. result.rs should be declared with the other modules at the top.

title: Provider name strings are hardcoded in multiple places per provider
why_it_matters: Each provider hardcodes its name in at least two places: the name() method and the SearchResult::provider field. These can drift out of sync.

title: No tests for provider search error handling
why_it_matters: All provider test modules only test construction. None test the search() method's error paths: HTTP errors, API error responses, JSON parse failures, or timeout handling.

title: TavilyProvider clones api_key on every search call
why_it_matters: TavilyRequest includes api_key: String which requires cloning the API key on every search invocation. Could use &str to avoid allocation.

title: Constructors should use impl Into<String> instead of String (8 occurrences)
why_it_matters: Project coding style requires constructors to accept impl Into<String> to reduce unnecessary allocations at call sites and provide a more ergonomic API.

title: Search query strings may leak PII/sensitive content through error logs
why_it_matters: Search queries are user-controlled and may contain PII. When a provider request fails, the registry logs the full error string which for GET-based providers may include the query parameter in the URL.
